description: Hi! Team Aetherion consists of 2 backend developers, one frontend web developer, a stats magician and a unicorn princess who writes really good team descriptions.
summary: The Rosenzweig index is a tool designed to bridge the gap for regular folks to be able to access and understand geospatial and earth science data. It harnesses the power of NASA Giovanni and AppEEARS to investigate patterns in data spanning over long periods of time. By helping identify changes in rainfall, temperature, and other environmental conditions, the project has potential value for farmers, who rely on these patterns when making decisions.
details:
The Rosenzweig Index is a web application that uses NASA Giovanni and AppEEARS.

Its main draws are:

  1. Paradox Finder checks for supported opposite trends within a region and shows cell trends even when none are found. Years-to-significance shows how evidence changes across historical records, not a future prediction. Our summaries come directly from computed results.
  2. Years-to-Significance estimates how many additional years of data might be needed for a trend to become statistically significant.
  3. Easy to use user interface to streamline the investigation process for non technical end users.

For the frontend, we used Typescript and React. For the backend, we used Python and fastAPI. To do data prototyping and statistical prototyping, we utilized Google Colab.

Note: At the time of writing, the latest deployment only supports the monthly rainfall parameter in Western Sahel
